_comment: ESP32-WROOM-32D on a generic devkit, with a VERIFIED 16 MB flash part.
There is no shipped manifest for this. The stock esp32dev board declares
4 MB, which is what a WROOM-32D usually carries and is not what is fitted
here -- and the module's printed name says nothing either way, which is
exactly why board_caps.cpp asks the chip at boot instead of trusting this
file. If esp_flash_get_physical_size() disagrees with the 16 MB below, the
firmware reports itself degraded and refuses to write past what is there.
maximum_size is the app0 partition from partitions/esp32_16mb_ota.csv, not
the flash size: it is the number the size check should be measured against,
because an image larger than one OTA slot cannot be installed even though
it would physically fit in the chip.
f_flash stays at the platform's conservative 40 MHz here and is raised to
80 MHz by the release environments, which is where the risk of a marginal
module belongs. flash_mode stays dio for the reason platformio.ini gives:
qio needs GPIO9/10 free and a board that has them wired does not boot at
name: ESP32-WROOM-32D (16 MB flash, no PSRAM)
